patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Salesforce Commerce Cloud and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Salesforce Commerce Cloud and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Salesforce Commerce Cloud only if your buying job matches “Salesforce B2C Commerce (ex-Demandware) — Growth/Plus/Premium are GMV-percent quote only; ” rather than WooCommerce's shape. Choose WooCommerce only if your buying job matches “Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and WooPaymen” rather than Salesforce Commerce Cloud's shape. Workflow advantage: Salesforce Commerce Cloud leans wholesale-b2b; WooCommerce leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Salesforce Commerce Cloud and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Salesforce Commerce Cloud is Salesforce B2C Commerce (ex-Demandware) — Growth/Plus/Premium are GMV-percent quote only; enterprise SaaS landscape, not an SMB Shopify subs; WooCommerce is Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and WooPayments processing are separate TCO lines..
- Company-size focus: Salesforce Commerce Cloud (mid-market, enterprise) vs WooCommerce (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: Salesforce Commerce Cloud-leaning wholesale-b2b vs WooCommerce-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Salesforce Commerce Cloud — Pricing is opaque GMV-% — hard to compare without a Salesforce worksheet; WooCommerce — You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS.

Limitations — Salesforce Commerce Cloud: Pricing is opaque GMV-% — hard to compare without a Salesforce worksheet; Implementation is a multi-month SI programme, not a weekend theme install; WooCommerce: You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS; Extension sprawl can inflate TCO and maintenance.

Poor-fit cases: Salesforce Commerce Cloud is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Pricing is opaque GMV-% — hard to compare without a Salesforce worksheet · WooCommerce is a poor fit when that limitation bites: You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS · Avoid Salesforce Commerce Cloud if you actually need WooCommerce's motion (Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
